turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): I must apologise, doctor. We are late. The auto was held up near the market, and then the lift was not working.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): That is quite all right, Mr. Iyer. Please sit. There is no hurry now.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The parking also, I tell you. We went round twice. Anyway, we are here.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. What has brought you in today?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Doctor, the reason I have come is bleeding from the gums. For three days, whenever I brush, there is blood, and I am rather worried.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): There are purple patches on his left forearm too. I saw them yesterday, umm, when I was helping with his shirt.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Bleeding from the gums for three days, and bruises on the left forearm since yesterday. Any black stools, or blood in the urine?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): No, doctor. Nothing of that kind. The motions and the urine are normal in colour.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain, or shortness of breath?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Breathing is comfortable, and there is no pain in the chest.
[SEG0011] person_4 (NURSE): Sir, the INR from this morning is 3.8. On the treatment card the warfarine is written as 5 mg at night.
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Excuse me, sister. I do not take 5 mg. I take 4 mg only, one yellow tablet by mouth after dinner. The 5 mg was right at the beginning.
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The card is an old one. At home the strip says 4 mg, and I am the one who gives it.

[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me say that back. The card says 5 mg at night, the two of you say 4 mg, and we cannot confirm the dose from what is in front of us. Today's INR is 3.8, above the usual 2 to 3.
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. I have had atrial fibrillation for about six years, and I have been on warfarine throughout.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. The fibrillation is longstanding, and the warfarin is for that. Has any new medicine been started anywhere else?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, err, three days back the doctor near our house started cifixime, 200 mg twice a day, for a urine infection. I am still taking it.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cefixime 200 mg twice daily, started three days ago, still going on, for a urinary infection. How is the burning now?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): The burning has settled, doctor. I am only finishing the tablets.

[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One more thing. I stopped his palak and methi last week. The neighbour said green leaves will make the blood too thick with this tablet. My sister takes biotin, 10 mg, for her hair fall, but that is her tablet, not his.

[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): We will not put your sister's biotin on his list. Less palak and methi means less vitamin K, and cefixime can lift the INR. That fits with 3.8 and the bleeding from the gums.
[SEG0022] person_4 (NURSE): Blood pressure just now is 142 over 84. Pulse is 92, and it is irregular.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): On examination the lower front gums are oozing a little, and I can see two bruises on the left forearm. The abdomen is soft. I do not see bleeding anywhere else.
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His elder brother had a stroke at sixty-eight. I thought you should know.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Please tell me how I should take the tablet from tonight. I will follow whatever you advise.

[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): My working impression is that the INR has risen from the antibiotic and from cutting down the greens, and that this is causing the gum bleeding and the bruises. Please take warfarin 3 mg once at night for the fibrillation, starting tonight.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): 3 mg once at night, from tonight. umm, should I stop the cifixime?

[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): No. Please finish the cefixime course the other doctor has given. And keep a small steady portion of palak or methi, rather than stopping the greens altogether or taking a large amount suddenly.
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): When do we repeat the blood test?
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): We will repeat the INR in one week. Kindly book it at the desk, and come back the same day with the report so that I can see you.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): In one week. Certainly, doctor. Is there anything I must watch for at home?

[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the bleeding becomes heavy, or the stools turn black, or there is a severe headache, go to casualty the same day. Do not wait for the visit. Otherwise I will review you in one week.

spec.situation: Older patient on warfarin for atrial fibrillation; INR result read aloud; antibiotic started elsewhere; green leafy diet changes; dose adjusted and recheck in a week.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: INR completed is supported, but nurse did not request it and indication wasn't stated.

omissions.text: Current warfarin dose was stated as 4 mg by mouth after dinner/at night (one yellow tablet), not just unspecified current warfarin use; the old treatment card listed 5 mg at night and this discrepancy could not be confirmed from available records.
Doctor advised the patient to come back the same day with the repeat INR report after booking the test at the desk.
Safety-net advice included not to wait for the visit if heavy bleeding, black stools, or severe headache occur; seek casualty the same day.
